name: Klaus-Michael Kuehne
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2003-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Logistics magnate Klaus-Michael Kuehne is honorary chairman of Kuehne + Nagel International AG, based in ‎Schindellegi‎, Switzerland.
He joined the company, cofounded by his grandfather, in 1958, eventually taking over as CEO in 1966.
In 2016, his Kuehne Holding AG acquired 20% of VTG, a rail logistics company. Two years later, it sold the stake to Morgan Stanley Infrastructure.
He owns roughly 30% of shipping and logistics company Hapag-Lloyd, a holding he has steadily increased in recent years.
Throughout the course of 2022, he acquired a 17.5% in Lufthansa, the German airline carrier, and became its largest single investor.
forbes_facts: Despite expressing frustration with the team's performance, Kuehne remains a minority owner of Hamburger SV, which plays in the second tier of pro soccer in Germany.
He transformed the 600-year old Castell Son Claret on Mallorca into a luxury hotel, and built another hotel, The Fontenay, in Hamburg.
Kuehne is an only child and has no children. His charitable foundation will continue to manage his wealth after he passes away.

name: Stefan Persson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (1996-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Stefan Persson is Sweden's richest person by way of global cheap chic fashion retailer Hennes & Mauritz, of which he owns almost 50%.
Persson stepped down as chairman in May 2020 after 22 years in the role; his son Karl-Johan succeeded him.
H&M was founded by Persson's father Erling in 1947.
Persson's two other children, Charlotte S'derstr?m and Tom Persson, and his sister Lottie Tham, are also billionaires.
forbes_facts: Persson personally owns real estate in some of the world's most glamorous shopping districts, spanning  New York, London, Rome and Paris.

name: Ken Fisher
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Ken Fisher is executive chairman and co-chief investment officer of Fisher Investments, which he founded in 1979 with $250.
The firm currently has more than $332 billion in assets under management.
In January 2025, Fisher sold a minority stake in Fisher Investments at a $12.75 billion valuation to buyout firm Advent and the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority.
In the summer of 1964, a 13-year-old Fisher earned $1.20 an hour picking fruit, sawing and fertilizing in his native San Mateo County, California.
Fisher dropped out of high school "because it was a waste of time" and headed to college where he could "take better classes."
forbes_facts: Fisher wrote an investing column in Forbes magazine for more than 32 years, penning his last one in late 2016.
Considered an expert on 19th century logging, Fisher has documented more than 35 abandoned logging camps in the northern Santa Cruz Mountains.

name: Nathan Blecharczyk
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2019-2023); Wikidata (2025); SEC insider holdings (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: Nathan Blecharczyk cofounded peer-to-peer room and home rental company Airbnb with Joe Gebbia and Brian Chesky in 2008.
Blecharczyk, who is chief strategy officer, was the company's first engineer. He is also the chairman of Airbnb China.
Airbnb now operates in over 100,000 cities in 220 countries. With more than 8 million listings worldwide, it has rented to 2 billion guests and counting.
Airbnb went public in a blockbuster IPO in 2020.
forbes_facts: His Airbnb cofounder Joe Gebbia brought on Blecharczyk, who was a former roommate in San Francisco, as chief technology officer.
Blecharczyk, who lives in San Francisco with his family, is an Airbnb host.

name: Thomas Pritzker
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Tom Pritzker is one of 13 billionaire heirs in the Pritzker clan behind hotel giant Hyatt.

He stepped down as Hyatt's executive chairman in February 2026 amid scrutiny over his friendly relationship with Jeffrey Epstein. "There is no excuse for failing to distance myself sooner," he said at the time.
Hyatt Hotels dates back to 1957 when Tom's father, Jay Pritzker (d. 1999), purchased the first Hyatt House motel near Los Angeles International Airport.
Tom's father Jay and uncle Robert acquired manufacturing firm Marmon in the 1950s and expanded it; Tom led Marmon's 2008 sale to Berkshire Hathaway.
Pritzker stepped down from the board of Royal Caribbean Cruises in 2020 after two decades as a director.
He founded the Pritzker Neuropsychiatric Disorders Research Consortium, a research effort into the genetic basis of psychiatric disorders.
forbes_facts: Pritzker is an Honorary Professor of History at Sichuan University in Chengdu, China.
Pritzker leads archeological expeditions in the Western Himalayas.

name: Leonid Boguslavsky
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Leonid Boguslavsky is founder of early stage venture capital firm  RTP Global, founded as ru-Net in 2000 in Russia.
One of his first investments was an early bet on Russian search engine firm Yandex, on which he apparently made 400 times his initial money upon exit.
RTP has invested in more than 150 companies, five of which became multibillion dollar public companies: Yandex, EPAM, Delivery Hero, RingCentral and Datadog.
In the early 1990s, he built one of Russia's largest IT solutions integrators, which he sold to PwC in 1996. He stayed on initially as a senior partner.
forbes_facts: Boguslavsky, who competed in his first triathlon at age 62, cofounded Super League Triathlon in 2017.

name: Michael Ashley
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Michael Ashley founded the U.K.'s largest sporting goods retailer, Sports Direct.
Ashley started Sports Direct in 1982 at age 18; it now has some 800 stores.
He took the company public in 2007, pocketing $1.8 billion from the IPO. That same year, he bought famed soccer club Newcastle United.
In 2021, Ashley sold Newcastle United to a consortium backed by Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund for around $400 million.
He renamed Sports Direct's parent company Frasers Group in 2019, after acquiring department store chain House of Fraser.
Ashley handed the CEO reins of Frasers Group to his son-in-law, Michael Murray, and stepped down from the Frasers board of directors in 2022.
forbes_facts: Ashley played squash growing up and reportedly dreamed of going pro, but his career was stopped short after an injury.

name: Frank Wang
forbes_bio: The world's first drone billionaire, Frank Wang is the founder and chairman of DJI, China's biggest seller of civil drones with over two-thirds market share.
Wang founded DJI in 2006 and ran it out of his dorm room at Hong Kong University of Science & Technology.
DJI is best known for its Phantom Drones, which retail for around $1,000.
DJI made a list of "Chinese military companies operating in the United States" published by the U.S. Department of Defense in 2022.
forbes_facts: The son of a teacher turned small-business owner, Wang spent most of his childhood reading about model airplanes.
When he was 16, Wang got a remote-controlled helicopter after getting high marks on an exam. He promptly crashed it and had to wait months for replacement parts.

name: Falguni Nayar
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun India (2018-2022)
forbes_bio: Former investment banker Falguni Nayar quit her job to start Nykaa, a retailer of beauty products in 2012.
Nykaa, which means "one in the spotlight," sells thousands of brands online as well through physical stores across India.
Nayar took Nykaa public in 2021, becoming India's richest self-made female entrepreneur in the process.
Her twin daughter and son both work in the business and have board seats.
Hong Kong billionaire Harry Banga is an investor in Nykaa.
forbes_facts: Nayar has an MBA from the elite Indian Institute of Management in Ahmedabad.
Nayar's husband Sanjay Nayar, the former CEO of KKR India, has cofounded venture capital firm Sorin Ventures.
In 2024, Nykaa entered the UAE under the Nysaa brand in a joint venture with Dubai's Apparel Group.

name: Scott Cook
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2003-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Scott Cook is the cofounder of financial software giant Intuit, known for products like QuickBooks, TurboTax and Mint.
The Harvard Business School grad worked for Procter & Gamble and Bain before launching Intuit in 1983.
He stepped down as CEO in 1994 and chairman in 1998 but remains a director and has a 2% stake.
Cook and his wife are big supporters of education and have donated millions to universities and are impact investors in several ed-tech funds.
Cook was planning to get a Ph.D. in economics but decided to pursue business after successfully turning his defunct college ski club into the biggest in the state.
forbes_facts: Cook was an early investor in Snapchat. He met cofounder Evan Spiegel after giving a guest lecture at Stanford.
Scott's son Karl Cook is a professional equestrian.

name: Andreas Martinos
forbes_bio: Andreas Martinos is the owner of Greek shipping firm Minerva Marine, which has a fleet of 75 tankers, dry cargo and container vessels.
He founded the company in 1998, after splitting from the family shipping company Thenamaris, which he had cofounded with his mother and two brothers in 1972.
Collectively, Andreas and his brothers Constantinos and Athanasios own the largest shipping fleet in Greece, the largest shipowning nation in the world.
Minerva Marine is now run by his son, also named Andreas.
